transcript.text: Hi Jordan, hi Rosa. As you both know, I've been holding onto Grandma's coin collection — all 42 coins — since she passed. I'm moving to a smaller apartment soon, so we really do need to settle what happens to the collection before then. Before I put together a final plan, I want to make sure I'm not missing anything. Is there anything either of you wants to mention — stories behind certain coins, things Grandma might have said, or any concerns — that you think should shape how I divide things up?
transcript.speaker: A1

transcript.text: Actually, yes — I got a written assessment last month from Helen Park, the family appraiser. She said the three 1909 Lincoln cents in the collection need to stay together and should be stored in acid-free capsules. I haven't had a chance to share this with everyone yet, but it seems important for the plan.

transcript.text: I have something to share too. I have a dated birthday card from Grandma where she promised me the 1921 Morgan silver dollar from the collection. I haven't shown it to either of you yet, but I think it's important to bring it up now so it can be part of the plan.

decisions.collection_plan: The collection of 42 coins will be divided as follows: Rosa will receive the 1921 Morgan silver dollar as Grandma promised her in writing. The three 1909 Lincoln cents will be kept together as a single lot and allocated to one recipient with proper storage. The remaining 38 coins will be divided equitably between Jordan and Rosa, with Maya recording who receives each individual item.
decisions.storage_plan: The three 1909 Lincoln cents must be stored together in acid-free capsules as recommended by appraiser Helen Park. Maya will ensure proper acid-free capsule storage is arranged for these coins before any transfer. All individual coin allocations will be documented in the final plan.

commitments.detail: Maya will record who receives each individual coin and small group from the collection as part of the final plan.
Maya will ensure the three 1909 Lincoln cents are stored together in acid-free capsules per Helen Park's assessment.
Rosa will receive the 1921 Morgan silver dollar as promised by Grandma in the dated birthday card.
